slots.label: Heading 1
slots.default: IT support in Newcastle: your questions answered

slots.label: Paragraph 1
slots.default: Not covered here? Ask us directly — same working day response.

slots.label: Question 1
slots.default: Do you have an office in Newcastle?

slots.label: Paragraph 2
slots.default: No. Our offices are at 124 City Rd in London and Caxton Point in Stevenage, and we are straight about that rather than listing a virtual address. Newcastle is covered by our UK service desk plus a team of field engineers who travel to customer sites. In practice most issues never need a visit at all: we respond the same working day and resolve most issues remotely. When a site visit is requested, we aim to have an engineer with you the same working day.

slots.label: Question 2
slots.default: Can you support several sites across the North East?

slots.label: Paragraph 3
slots.default: Yes, and multi-site is one of the patterns we handle best. One service desk, one set of standards and the same monitoring and patching across every location, with engineers dispatched to whichever site needs someone physically present. You get consistency instead of each office quietly doing its own thing.

slots.label: Question 3
slots.default: We already have someone handling IT internally. Can you work alongside them?

slots.label: Paragraph 4
slots.default: Frequently, yes. A common arrangement is that we absorb the day-to-day tickets, monitoring and patching so your internal person is freed up for projects and the things only they can do. We can also cover holidays and act as escalation only, if that is all you need.

slots.label: Question 4
slots.default: How do you approach cyber security?

slots.label: Paragraph 5
slots.default: We are Cyber Essentials Certified ourselves rather than simply aligned to it, and we take clients through the same certification. Beyond that the practical work is email security, endpoint protection, patching, multi-factor authentication and tested backups.

slots.label: Paragraph 6
slots.default: We start with an assessment of your current systems and what the business actually needs, agree a support plan, deploy the tooling we use for remote assistance, monitoring and patching, then go live. You get a named point of contact rather than a ticket portal and nothing else.
